1.title: DAX Basics: Measures, Filter Context and CALCULATE
1.text: Welcome to Module six: dacks Basics: Measures, Filter Context and calculate. It covers the exam area Model the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Create single aggregation measures. Use the calculate function. Create a measure by using quick measures. Create calculated tables or columns. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Model the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Measures and aggregation functions
1.text: Measures and aggregation functions. A measure is a dacks formula that is calculated at query time, once for every cell of a visual, using the filters that apply to that cell.

1.title: Measures and aggregation functions, continued
1.text: Measures and aggregation functions. The figure shows this: A matrix cell and the filters from its row, its column and a slicer that form the filter context of a measure.

1.title: Measures and aggregation functions, continued
1.text: Measures and aggregation functions. sum. The total of the numbers in a column. average. The mean of the numbers in a column. count. How many numbers or dates a column holds (count A counts any non-blank value). count rows. How many rows a table has. distinct count. How many different values a column holds. min and max. The smallest and the largest value. divide. A division that returns blank, or an alternate result you give, instead of an error when the divisor is zero. sum X, average X, max X. Iterators: evaluate an expression for each row of a table, then aggregate the results.

1.title: Measures and aggregation functions, continued
1.text: Measures and aggregation functions. An implicit measure appears when you drag a numeric column into a visual and Power B I aggregates it with the default summarization. An explicit measure is a measure you write in dacks. Prefer explicit measures: other measures can reuse them, results stay consistent, and calculation groups work only with them. The model setting Discourage implicit measures enforces this.

1.title: Measures and aggregation functions, continued
1.text: Measures and aggregation functions. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Measures and aggregation functions, continued
1.text: Measures and aggregation functions. Use sum X when the value needs a calculation on each row first. sum of Quantity times sum of Unit Price gives a different, wrong answer. Exam tip: Use divide instead of the slash operator to avoid divide-by-zero errors. count counts values in a column, count rows counts table rows, distinct count counts unique values. Exam tip: A function ending in X is an iterator. It calculates row by row and then aggregates, so use it when the formula combines several columns of one row.

1.title: Filter context and row context
1.text: Filter context and row context. Filter context decides which rows are visible; row context points at one row inside them. Filter context. What it is: The set of filters in force while a measure is evaluated; it limits the rows each table exposes. Where it exists: Every cell of a visual: its rows and columns, slicers, report filters, relationships and calculate. Row context. What it is: The current row of one table, so a formula can read that row's columns. Where it exists: Calculated columns and the X iterator functions.

1.title: Filter context and row context, continued
1.text: Filter context and row context. A measure such as sum(Sales Amount) has no current row. It adds up whatever rows survive the filter context, so each cell of a matrix gets its own answer. Filters on a dimension pass through relationships from the one side to the many side (see Module five). Row context does not filter other tables. When calculate runs inside a row context, it turns the current row into filters. This is called context transition. It is also why a measure that you call inside a calculated column or an iterator works for each row. Exam tip: Calculated columns and iterators create row context; measures are evaluated in filter context. calculate is the function that changes filter context, and inside a row context it converts the row into filters.

1.title: CALCULATE and variables
1.text: calculate and variables. calculate ( expression, filter one, filter two,... ) evaluates the expression after it changes the filter context with the filter arguments. Several filter arguments combine with and. A filter on a different column adds to the existing filters; a filter on the same column replaces the existing one.

1.title: CALCULATE and variables, continued
1.text: calculate and variables. Boolean filter, such as Product Color equals "Red". Replaces any filter on that column; it can use only one column and cannot call a measure. filter. Table filter for a condition that uses several columns or a measure. all. Removes filters from a table or from the columns you list. remove filters. Does the same as all, but only inside calculate, and says what it means.

1.title: CALCULATE and variables, continued
1.text: calculate and variables. all selected. Removes the filters of the visual but keeps the outer ones, such as slicers; used for percent of the selection. all except. Removes all filters of a table except on the columns you list. keep filters. Adds the new filter to the existing ones instead of replacing them. Exam tip: keep filters intersects with the existing filter instead of overwriting it. Use filter when a condition needs a measure or more than one column.

1.title: CALCULATE and variables, continued
1.text: calculate and variables. A variable is declared with var and the result is given with return. It is evaluated once, where it is defined, and does not change when a later calculate changes the context. Variables make a measure faster to run and easier to read. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A Boolean filter in calculate replaces the existing filter on that column. all and remove filters remove filters; all selected keeps slicer selections, so it is the choice for a percent of what the user selected.

1.title: Quick measures
1.text: Quick measures. A quick measure is a dialog on the Home tab that writes the dacks for you. You choose a calculation, drag fields into the boxes, and Power B I creates an ordinary explicit measure that you can read and edit afterwards. Aggregate per category. Average, minimum, maximum or weighted average per category. Filters. A filtered value, or the difference from a filtered value. Time intelligence. Year-to-date, quarter-to-date and month-to-date totals, year-over-year change, rolling average. Totals. Running total. Mathematical operations. Addition, subtraction, division, percentage difference. Text. Star rating, concatenated list of values.

2.title: Quick measures, continued
2.text: Quick measures. The time intelligence quick measures cannot be used in Direct Query. Quick measures are a good way to learn the dacks pattern, but the exam expects you to recognize the result, not to type it from memory. Exam tip: Quick measures create regular dacks measures, and the time intelligence category does not work with Direct Query. Use them to build a running total or a year-over-year change without writing dacks.

2.title: Calculated columns and calculated tables
2.text: Calculated columns and calculated tables. Module five explains when to choose each object. Here is how they behave in dacks. Calculated column. Context: Row context; stored in the model and computed at refresh. Key function: related fetches one value from the one side of a relationship. Calculated table. Context: A table expression, stored in the model. Key function: calendar auto, union or a copy of a table.

2.title: Calculated columns and calculated tables, continued
2.text: Calculated columns and calculated tables. For example, a calculated column in Sales that is defined as related of Product Category gives every sales row the category of its product. related follows the relationship to the one side and returns one value. related table goes the other way and returns the related rows of the many side. Both need a relationship. Power Query is preferred when the logic can be done there. Create a column with New column on the Table tools tab, and a table with New table. Exam tip: related returns a single value from the one side; related table returns the many-side rows. Both depend on an existing relationship and a row context.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. The Sales table has Quantity and Unit Price columns but no revenue column. A card must show total revenue. Which measure should you write? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: sum X over Sales, multiplying Quantity by Unit Price. sum X multiplies the two columns on each row before it adds the results, whereas the other options combine totals or averages.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. An author drags the Amount column onto a card and gets a sum. The team later wants to reuse the calculation in other measures and in a calculation group. What should the author create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An explicit measure that sums the Amount column. An explicit measure is named, reusable and the only kind that a calculation group can change.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Each Sales row must show the category of its product, which is stored in the Product table. A relationship exists between the tables. Which function should the calculated column use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The related function on the Product Category. related follows the relationship to the one side and returns a single value for the current row.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A measure must total sales for all product categories even when a Category slicer is set. Region slicers must still apply. Which pattern should you use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: calculate with remove filters on Product Category. remove filters on the Category column clears only that filter, while the other filters still apply.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A percent-of-total measure must divide by the total of the products that are shown in the visual after the slicers apply. What should the denominator use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: calculate with all selected on the Product table. all selected clears the filters of the visual but keeps the slicer selections, which gives the total of what the user selected.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A model uses Direct Query. An author tries to create a year-over-year change quick measure. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: It is not available because the model uses Direct Query. Time intelligence quick measures cannot be used with Direct Query.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which function counts the unique values in a column? Answer: distinct count. Question two. Which two kinds of formula create a row context? Answer: Calculated columns and iterator (X) functions. Question three. Which function avoids a divide-by-zero error? Answer: divide.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What do var and return do? Answer: var stores a value once, and return gives the result of the measure. Question five. What does keep filters do inside calculate? Answer: It keeps the existing filters and adds the new one instead of replacing them. Question six. What does a quick measure produce? Answer: An ordinary dacks measure that you can edit.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Aggregations: sum, average, count, count rows, distinct count, min, max; divide is the safe division. Iterators: X functions such as sum X work row by row, then aggregate. Explicit and implicit: Explicit measures are written in dacks and reusable; Discourage implicit measures enforces them. Filter context: The filters in force for a cell; row context is the current row. calculate: Changes the filter context; same column replaces, different column adds. Modifiers: all and remove filters remove; all selected keeps slicers; all except; keep filters intersects. Variables: var and return; evaluated once. Quick measures: Home tab dialog that writes dacks; time intelligence not in Direct Query. Calculated column: Row context; related (one side value) and related table (many-side rows).
